# LLMs.txt - Cyclops

Guidance for LLM agents working on or with this project. Read this before
touching the code; most of the non-obvious landmines are documented here.

## What this is

Cyclops is a Windows 11 utility that exposes a Windows Hello IR camera two
ways: a Qt GUI with live preview + illuminator toggle, and an optional
Media Foundation virtual camera that any app can open. MIT licensed. Only
hardware-verified target: NexiGo HelloCam N930W (USB `VID_2B7E&PID_C569`,
IR interface `MI_02`, 640x360 L8 @ ~30fps).

## Repo map

- `src/ir_capture.{hpp,cpp}` - MF `IMFSourceReader` capture + FACEAUTH
  extended camera control. Shared by the exe AND the vcam DLL.
- `src/capture_worker.hpp` - `QThread` owning an `ir_capture`; emits `QImage`
  frames to the GUI. `open()` must reset `cancel_` (a previous `stop()`
  leaves it set, which silently skips the read loop).
- `src/main_window.{hpp,cpp}` - Qt GUI. Restarts are debounced 50ms through
  `schedule_restart()`; do not call `restart_capture()` directly from
  multiple paths (a `stop()` landing mid-open strands the preview).
- `src/vcam_manager.{hpp,cpp}` - device lifecycle: install/uninstall
  (elevated helper re-launch via `ShellExecuteEx runas`), enable/disable.
- `src/vcam_ids.hpp` - shared constants: CLSID, friendly name, install dir
  (`%ProgramData%\Cyclops`, resolved at runtime), flag/log filenames.
- `src/vcam_flag.hpp` - one-byte `illuminator` flag file; the cross-process
  control channel between the GUI and the Frame Server-hosted media source.
- `vcam/` - `CyclopsVcamSource.dll`: hand-rolled COM (no winrt::implements;
  the SDK cppwinrt doesn't forward interface methods). `vcam_activator`
  (IMFActivate) -> `vcam_source` (IMFMediaSourceEx) -> `vcam_stream`
  (IMFMediaStream2 + IKsControl). `vcam_com.hpp` holds `attr_forwarder`
  (IMFAttributes delegation) and `server_lock` counting for
  `DllCanUnloadNow`.

## Invariants you must not break

1. **`KSCAMERA_EXTENDEDPROP_FACEAUTH_MODE_DISABLED` is `0x1`, not `0`.**
   `illumination_on()` is `mode > DISABLED`. Treating any nonzero mode as
   "on" makes the emitter impossible to re-enable.
2. **IR sensor cameras are invisible to DirectShow.** Always enumerate
   `KSCATEGORY_SENSOR_CAMERA` via `MFEnumDeviceSources`.
3. **`MFStartup` is required before `IMFVirtualCamera` methods.** Without
   it, `Start` can still succeed but `Stop`/`Remove`/`GetEvent` return
   `MF_E_SHUTDOWN`, and `enum_video_cameras()` silently returns empty.
4. **Samples must come from the client-provided `IMFVideoSampleAllocator`.**
   `GetAllocatorUsage` advertises `UsesProvidedAllocator`; `RequestSample`
   queues onto `pending_` and the pump fulfills one per fresh camera frame -
   answering synchronously lets Frame Server free-run the pipeline at
   thousands of fps. Self-allocated buffers can't cross to the client.
5. **`cap_` (ir_capture) is owned by the pump thread.** Never call it from
   stream/source methods; route control through the flag file.
6. **Never hold `lock_` across `GetEvent` or pump joins** - `GetEvent(0)`
   blocks until an event exists; a queued MEMediaSample may be what it waits
   for. Snapshot COM pointers under the lock, call outside. Pump joins are
   serialized by `join_mu_` and bounded at 5s (`join_pump`); a wedged
   ReadSample gets the pump *abandoned*, never TerminateThread - a killed
   thread can orphan MF-internal locks and deadlock Frame Server. The pump
   self-refs the stream so it can't outlive its members, frees `cap_` on
   exit, and `cap_abandoned_` permanently fails that stream's Start. Backoff
   sleeps wait on `stop_event_` so Stop/Shutdown wake immediately, and Start
   must ResetEvent it (manual-reset). `shutdown_` blocks Start re-entry once
   Shutdown begins. Start joins a previous pump *before* taking `lock_` and
   only from STOPPED; PAUSED still has a live pump, so Stop (stream and
   source) treats it like RUNNING.
7. **Removal contract: `Remove()` then `Shutdown()` on a fresh binding, no
   `Start`, no `AddDeviceSourceInfo`.** `Stop` only works on the object that
   called `Start`; `AddDeviceSourceInfo` on a removal binding makes `Remove`
   fail.
8. **`MFCreateVirtualCamera` is create-or-open** keyed on (friendly name,
   source CLSID, lifetime, access). Calling it just to remove a device will
   create a phantom - enumerate first, remove only what exists.
9. **The `%ProgramData%\Cyclops` ACL model is split by role and protected.**
   Dir: BU/LS read+execute+create-files, no delete-child, no ProgramData
   inheritance; DLL: BU/LS read+execute only, `D:P`; flag/log: BU/LS
   read+write+delete. Owner is Administrators everywhere - an object owned
   by a user keeps implicit WRITE_DAC. `ir_log` never creates the dir (a
   user-context creation would leave it weakly secured), and flag/log
   access refuses hardlinks/reparse points so a user can't turn a
   LocalService write into an arbitrary file primitive. The flag file is
   fail-closed: missing or unreadable means emitter off, and install seeds
   it off (the pump commits it for any vcam client, Cyclops running or not).
   The elevated install refuses a pre-existing dir that is a reparse point:
   a user can plant a junction there and redirect the DLL Frame Server loads.
10. **`attr_forwarder`'s store is never nulled after creation** (shutdown
    paths included) - in-flight attribute calls would dangle.
11. **Physical-camera teardown has exactly one owner.** Normally the
    activator (ShutdownObject for the associated activation, Shutdown for
    self-opened sources); `DetachObject` hands ownership to the stream via
    `adopt_physical`, which runs it in the stream's own Shutdown; a stream
    that already shut down refuses the handoff and the activator tears down
    itself. **Frame Server releases the activator right after
    ActivateObject and keeps only the source**, so the activator dtor is
    the same handoff, never a teardown: shutting the camera (or the source)
    down there makes every associated-source open fail. The stream only
    calls `physical_->Stop()` when it doesn't own teardown. **The pump
    opens the sensor directly by the persisted symlink first**: the
    associated (proxy) source streams but exposes no illuminating FACEAUTH
    mode on the N930W, so it is only the fallback for a sensor we can't
    open by name. The activator therefore always reads `symlink_attr`.
12. **`ir_capture` must disconnect adopted sources on reader shutdown.**
    `MF_SOURCE_READER_DISCONNECT_MEDIASOURCE_ON_SHUTDOWN` keeps reader
    release from calling `Shutdown()` on a Frame-Server-associated source
    the activator still owns - without it every `cap_.close()` poisons the
    associated camera permanently.
13. **Advertise NV12 only.** MF RGB32 crosses the DirectShow bridge as
    `BI_RGB` with a negative `biHeight`, which infinite-loops Discord's
    aspect-ratio reducer. `tools/dshow_enum.exe` enumerates the exposed
    types without starting capture - run it after any format change and
    confirm no negative heights. The advertised size and rate come from
    `probe_source_geometry` (ir_capture), the same stream pick and rounding
    the pump's capture uses; the type is fixed at Initialize, so a capture
    of another size is logged and delivered black or sheared.
14. **Capture metadata is typed `UINT64`.**
    `MF_CAPTURE_METADATA_FRAME_ILLUMINATION` must be read with `GetUINT64`
    (tolerating `GetUINT32` drivers); a `GetUINT32` read always fails and
    silently disables metadata strobe detection. The off-phase drop is
    gated on `strobing_` - an ungated drop discards every frame on a
    metadata-tagging driver with the emitter off.

## Frame Server operational notes

- The loaded DLL image is cached per-process. Replacing or renaming the file
  does not affect already-mapped code. To load a new build: close all camera
  clients, then `--vcam-disable` + `--vcam-enable`, or restart the
  `FrameServer` service (elevated). `vcam dll unloaded` in the log confirms
  release.
- A System-lifetime device can drop out of enumeration when Frame Server
  restarts. The GUI self-heals: `webcam_desired_` persists in QSettings
  (`webcam_on`), and `refresh_webcam_status` re-runs `enable()` (bounded, 3
  attempts) when a desired device is missing. `enable()` is idempotent.
- `MFVirtualCameraAccess_CurrentUser` binds the device to the installing
  token's user; over-the-shoulder UAC (admin approving for a standard user)
  registers it under the wrong account. The unelevated `enable()` self-heals
  by creating the desktop user's own device; `install_main` logs the
  mismatch.
- `KsProperty` is read-only toward the physical camera: GET/BASICSUPPORT
  forward, SET only ever touches the virtual FACEAUTH flag. A vcam client
  must never mutate hardware shared with Windows Hello.
- `RequestSample` only fires while a client is actively streaming. No client,
  no samples - silence is not a bug.
- Stale `CyclopsVcamSource.old*.dll` files are expected residue; uninstall
  sweeps them.

## Debug

- Everything logs to `%ProgramData%\Cyclops\cyclops.log` via `ir_log()`
  (both the exe and the FS-hosted DLL write it). Key lines:
  `gui: capture opened` / `gui: first frame delivered`,
  `vcam stream started, fmt=..., allocator=...`, `vcam: first RequestSample`,
  `IR emitter on/off`, `vcam dll unloaded`.
- FACEAUTH SETs from client apps arrive via `IKsControl::KsProperty` and are
  routed to the flag file - they apply even before the stream runs.

## Testing

No unit tests; verification is a live hardware pass:

1. `cmake --build build --config Release`
2. Launch `build\Release\cyclops.exe`: preview shows the IR feed.
3. Flip **IR illuminator** off/on: feed darkens/brightens; log shows
   `IR emitter off`/`IR emitter on` (not `IR emitter on` twice).
4. Flip **Windows webcam**: device enumerates as "Cyclops (Windows Hello
   camera passthrough)"; open it in Camera app/OBS -> live frames.
5. `tools\dshow_enum.exe` (build with `tools\build_enum.bat`): must list
   only positive-height types for Cyclops. The source advertises NV12 only;
   the DirectShow bridge synthesizes YUY2 from it, so YUY2 + NV12 at
   640x360 is the expected listing. Any negative `biHeight` reintroduces
   the Discord CPU loop.
6. `--vcam-disable` then `--vcam-enable`: device disappears/returns.
7. `--vcam-uninstall` (elevated): CLSID key and `%ProgramData%\Cyclops` gone.
